rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: The UAE registers left-hand-drive vehicles only. Right-hand-drive vehicles are generally not permitted for private registration unless converted to LHD.

rules.title: No general age limit
rules.rule_text: There is no universal age limit for importing used cars into the UAE, but vehicles must meet GCC specification and older vehicles may require additional approval in some emirates. Confirm with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: GCC specification required
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles should conform to GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) specification. Non-GCC-specification vehicles may require modification before registration.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV incentives
rules.rule_text: The UAE offers incentives for electric vehicles including public charging programs and toll exemptions in some emirates. Confirm current EV import requirements with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Saudi Arabia is a left-hand-drive market. Vehicles must be LHD to be registered.

rules.title: Used passenger car age limit (5 years)
rules.rule_text: Saudi Arabia generally restricts import of used passenger cars to those no older than five years; heavy vehicles may have different limits. Confirm with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: SABER / SASO conformity
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles require SASO conformity and registration on the SABER platform before shipment.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV adoption incentives
rules.rule_text: Saudi Arabia is promoting EV adoption through charging infrastructure and fee exemptions. Confirm current EV import rules with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Kenya is a right-hand-drive market. Vehicles must be RHD to be registered under KS 1515.

rules.title: 8-year age limit
rules.rule_text: Kenya limits import of used motor vehicles to those not older than eight years, enforced under KS 1515:2000. Confirm the exact cut-off with official customs (KRA/KEBS) before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-shipment inspection (PVoC)
rules.rule_text: Used vehicles require a Pre-Export Verification of Conformity (PVoC) certificate before export to Kenya.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV duty relief
rules.rule_text: Kenya applies a reduced import duty and exempts electric vehicles from excise duty under the EAC Common External Tariff. Confirm current rates with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Tanzania is a right-hand-drive market. Vehicles must be RHD to be registered.

rules.title: Age limit (about 8-10 years)
rules.rule_text: Tanzania restricts import of used vehicles by age, commonly around eight to ten years. Confirm the current limit with official customs (TRA) before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-shipment inspection (PVoC)
rules.rule_text: Used vehicles require a Pre-shipment Verification of Conformity (PVoC) through the Tanzania Bureau of Standards before import.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV incentives
rules.rule_text: Tanzania has introduced incentives to encourage EV imports, including reduced excise on electric vehicles. Confirm current policy with official authorities before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Nigeria is a right-hand-drive market. Left-hand-drive vehicles are generally not permitted for registration.

rules.title: Vehicle age restriction
rules.rule_text: Nigeria restricts import of used vehicles by age, and the rules have changed in recent years. Confirm current limits with official customs (Nigeria Customs Service) before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-shipment inspection (SONCAP / Form M)
rules.rule_text: Used vehicles are subject to Nigeria's import clearance and pre-shipment inspection requirements (SONCAP / Form M). Confirm current procedure with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV policy developing
rules.rule_text: Nigeria's EV import policy is developing, with discussion of duty relief for electric vehicles. Confirm current rules with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Kazakhstan is a left-hand-drive market. Right-hand-drive vehicles are generally not permitted.

rules.title: Vehicle age limit (recently adjusted)
rules.rule_text: Kazakhstan applies an age limit to imported used vehicles, which has been adjusted in recent years. Confirm the current limit with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EAEU technical regulations
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must comply with EAEU (Eurasian Economic Union) technical regulations and certification.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV duty exemption
rules.rule_text: Kazakhstan has temporarily exempted electric vehicles from customs duty and recycling fee to promote adoption. Confirm current status with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Uzbekistan is a left-hand-drive market. Vehicles must be LHD to be registered.

rules.title: Strict import controls
rules.rule_text: Uzbekistan applies strict controls on vehicle imports, including certification and recycling fees. Confirm current requirements with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Vehicle age restrictions
rules.rule_text: Uzbekistan has historically restricted used vehicle imports by age. Confirm current limits with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: EV import duty & excise exemption
rules.rule_text: Uzbekistan exempts electric vehicles from import duty and excise tax to encourage adoption. Confirm current rates with official customs before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with official authorities before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: South Africa drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. Left-hand-drive vehicles are generally not registrable for private use.

rules.title: ITAC import permit required
rules.rule_text: Used/second-hand vehicles may only be imported with an International Trade Administration Commission (ITAC) import permit. Permits are restricted mainly to returning South African nationals, permanent-residence immigrants, racing cars, vintage, specially designed and inherited vehicles.

rules.title: NRCS Letter of Authority + Interpol clearance
rules.rule_text: SARS requires, for a second-hand vehicle import to be legal: customs clearance documents, a Letter of Authority from the National Regulator for Compulsory Specifications (NRCS), an ITAC import permit, and an Interpol clearance certificate.

rules.title: No fixed age limit (restricted categories)
rules.rule_text: South Africa has no hard age cut-off for used vehicles, but imports are restricted to defined permit categories (returning residents, immigrants, special-purpose vehicles). Confirm current ITAC permit eligibility before sourcing stock.
rules.notes: Permit categories are restrictive — verify eligibility with ITAC before purchase.

rules.title: EVs face 25% import duty (no relief)
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles attract the same 25% passenger-vehicle import duty (higher than the 18% ICE rate in some classifications); there is no EV-specific import-duty relief in South Africa.
rules.notes: Confirm current HS 87 duty classification with SARS before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Egypt drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are not registrable — typical RHD Japanese used cars cannot be imported or registered.

rules.title: Used cars near-new (about 1 year); EVs up to 3 years
rules.rule_text: Egypt restricts used passenger-car imports to near-new units (about one year old), while electric vehicles up to three years old are permitted under the 2025 EV policy.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Egyptian Customs before purchase.

rules.title: NAFEZA single-window clearance
rules.rule_text: All vehicle shipments must clear through the NAFEZA single-window system; import licence, certificate of conformity and proof of payment via authorised banks are required.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Egyptian Customs before purchase.

rules.title: EV import duty exemption (0%)
rules.rule_text: From 1 January 2025 Egypt exempts pure-electric vehicles (BEV, HS 8703.80) from customs duty (0%), with a progressive FOB-value deduction up to 50%. Individuals may import one EV every five years.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Egyptian Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Jordan drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: EV age cap of 3 years
rules.rule_text: Under rules effective 1 November 2025, electric vehicles more than three years old (including the year of customs clearance) may no longer be imported.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Jordan Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Salvage / damaged vehicles banned
rules.rule_text: Vehicles classified as salvage or junk — including fire-, flood-damaged or unrepairable units — may no longer be imported into Jordan.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Jordan Customs before purchase.

rules.title: EV special tax unified at 27%
rules.rule_text: Under the 2025 Special Tax Bylaw (announced 28 June 2025), special tax on electric vehicles is unified at 27% for all categories, versus 51% for petrol and 39% for hybrid vehicles.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Jordan Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Pakistan drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Cars up to 3 years (personal schemes)
rules.rule_text: Under the Personal Baggage, Gift and Transfer of Residence schemes, used cars not older than 3 years and other vehicles not older than 5 years may be imported. The commercial-channel 5-year age cap was removed from 1 July 2026 (SRO 1065/2026).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with FBR before purchase.

rules.title: Personal Baggage / Gift / Transfer of Residence schemes
rules.rule_text: Used vehicles are imported by overseas Pakistanis under the Personal Baggage, Gift or Transfer of Residence schemes only; duty is a fixed US-dollar schedule by engine capacity (e.g. US$13,200 for 1001–1300cc).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with FBR before purchase.

rules.title: EV duty concession (25% up to US$50k)
rules.rule_text: Electric 4-wheelers valued up to US$50,000 are taxed at 25% customs duty; hybrid electric vehicles up to 1800cc receive a 50% duty exemption (25% for 1800–2500cc).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with FBR before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Bangladesh drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Reconditioned-car age restrictions
rules.rule_text: Bangladesh imports reconditioned (used) vehicles under NBR rules with age and condition restrictions; duty is a compounding cascade of customs duty, supplementary duty, VAT, advance income tax and regulatory duty.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with NBR before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-export inspection required
rules.rule_text: Reconditioned vehicle imports require pre-export inspection and standard documentation (invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with NBR before purchase.

rules.title: PHEV / EV duty reduction
rules.rule_text: Bangladesh has proposed import-duty cuts on plug-in hybrid electric vehicles as part of its energy-efficiency strategy; EV/PHEV duty treatment is evolving.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with NBR before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Chile drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: No import age limit
rules.rule_text: Chile has no import age limit for used vehicles, making it one of the most flexible markets in Latin America.
rules.notes: Confirm current SNA customs rules before ordering used units.

rules.title: RUT + standard documents
rules.rule_text: A Chilean tax identification number (RUT) is required; clearance needs the invoice, bill of lading, certificate of origin and export certificate.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Chile Customs before purchase.

rules.title: No EV-specific duty relief
rules.rule_text: Chile applies a flat 6% ad valorem duty regardless of powertrain; no EV-specific import-duty relief is recorded. Chinese EVs have strong market presence.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Chile Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Thailand drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. China-market LHD units cannot be registered as-is; source RHD export units.

rules.title: Used-vehicle imports tightly restricted
rules.rule_text: Thailand heavily restricts used-vehicle imports. Regular used passenger-car imports are generally not permitted for private registration; only new cars and limited special categories (classic vehicles 30+ years, returning residents) may qualify. Verify current rules with Thai Customs.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Thai Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Import permit (Department of Foreign Trade)
rules.rule_text: New-vehicle imports require an import permit from the Department of Foreign Trade and conformity with Thai emissions and safety standards. Confirm the full permit and clearance procedure before shipping.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Thai Customs before purchase.

rules.title: EV 3.5 package (excise 8%→2%)
rules.rule_text: Under the EV 3.5 package, battery-electric passenger cars priced up to 7 million baht receive an excise-tax reduction from 8% to 2%, and CBU EV imports during 2024–2025 benefit from reduced import duty. Confirm current rates with Thai Customs/BOI.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Thai Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Vietnam drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles — which rules out the large RHD used-car pipelines of Japan and Thailand and favors China-sourced LHD units.

rules.title: 5-year age limit (Decree 116/2017)
rules.rule_text: Under Decree 116/2017/ND-CP, imported used passenger cars must generally be no more than 5 years from the year of manufacture — a firm cutoff, not a guideline. In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2021 and newer.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Vietnam Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Type approval + used-car surcharge
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles require type approval and technical safety inspection; used combustion cars also face a fixed mixed-duty surcharge on top of import duty, special consumption tax and VAT. Confirm documents and the surcharge with Vietnam Customs.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Vietnam Customs before purchase.

rules.title: EV incentive (0% duty + 3% SCT)
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles enjoy 0% import duty and a reduced 3% special consumption tax under the current incentive window (running into early 2027) — a structural advantage over combustion used imports.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Vietnam Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Indonesia drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Used-car imports effectively prohibited
rules.rule_text: Indonesia effectively prohibits the import of used (second-hand) vehicles — only new completely built-up (CBU) units may be imported under an importer licence (API) with type approval, and even those are restricted to protect local assembly.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Indonesian customs before purchase.

rules.title: CBU EV duty exemption (until Dec 2025)
rules.rule_text: Indonesia exempted CBU battery-electric cars from import duty and reduced the luxury-goods sales tax (PPnBM) until 31 December 2025; the Industry Ministry has announced the CBU EV incentive will not continue in 2026.
rules.source: Schinder Law Firm / Indonesia Industry Ministry
rules.notes: CBU EV incentive ends Dec 2025 — verify current status with Indonesian customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Mexico drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Eight-year rule for definitive used import
rules.rule_text: Used passenger cars imported as definitive imports generally must have a model year within the last eight years; older units face additional hurdles, higher taxes or prohibition. Border-zone temporary import programs have their own age windows.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Mexican customs (Aduanas/SAT) before purchase.

rules.title: NOM conformity (emissions & safety)
rules.rule_text: Definitively imported vehicles must satisfy Mexican Official Standards (NOM) for emissions and safety; US/Canada-origin vehicles follow the border and decree procedures. Confirm the applicable NOM conformity path before shipment.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Mexican customs before purchase.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief is recorded for Mexico; imported vehicles face standard duty plus 16% IVA. Mexico has separate EV market incentives, but these do not reduce used-vehicle import duty.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Mexican customs before purchase.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Ghana drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 15-year age limit (from 1 Oct 2026)
rules.rule_text: Under the Ghana Standards Authority's National Vehicle Homologation and Conformity Assessment Programme, effective 1 October 2026, used vehicles older than 15 years are refused entry; vehicles 10–15 years old may attract overage penalties. In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2011 and newer.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with GSA before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-shipment inspection + Certificate of Conformity
rules.rule_text: Every used vehicle must be inspected in its country of origin by a GSA-approved inspection organisation before shipment; a cleared unit receives a Certificate of Conformity confirming safety, quality and environmental compliance.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with GSA before purchase.

rules.title: EV import-duty reduction (developing)
rules.rule_text: Ghana has moved to reduce import duty on electric vehicles as part of its energy-transition policy; EV duty treatment is evolving and should be confirmed with the Ghana Revenue Authority before trading.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with GRA before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Peru drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 5-year age limit (2 years for diesel)
rules.rule_text: Peru limits used-vehicle imports to 5 years old for spark-ignition (petrol) vehicles and 2 years old for compression-ignition (diesel) vehicles; age is counted from the year of manufacture to shipment date.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with SUNAT before purchase.

rules.title: Ad valorem + ISC + IGV layered taxes
rules.rule_text: Vehicle imports face ad valorem CIF customs duty, selective consumption tax (ISC) on duty-inclusive value, and general sales tax (IGV 17%) plus municipal promotion tax (IPM 2%) on the cumulative base. Clearance is via the Unique Customs Declaration (DUA).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with SUNAT before purchase.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief is recorded for Peru; EVs are subject to the same ad valorem duty and IGV/IPM as combustion vehicles. Confirm current treatment with SUNAT.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with SUNAT before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: The Philippines drives on the right and requires left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Importing a right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicle is a criminal offence under Republic Act No. 8506.

rules.title: Used-vehicle imports generally prohibited (NDI exceptions)
rules.rule_text: Under EO 156 as amended by EO 877-A, import of used motor vehicles is generally prohibited. Limited exceptions exist under the No-Dollar Importation (NDI) program for returning residents (≥1 year abroad), immigrants (13g/13a visas), and diplomats. The vehicle must be owned and registered ≥6 months, one unit per family, and cannot be resold for 3 years.

rules.title: EV zero import duty (EO 12, extended to 2028)
rules.rule_text: Executive Order No. 12 (s.2023) temporarily zero-rates import duty on electric vehicles, parts and components; the NEDA Board extended it to 2028 and broadened it to cover hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs) and plug-in hybrids, removing the previous 30% duty on hybrids/PHEVs.
rules.source: HKTDC Research / Bureau of Customs CMC 64-2023
rules.notes: Temporary measure extended to 2028 — verify current status with the Bureau of Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Iraq drives on the right and requires left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Non-armored vehicles only; salvage, flood- and fire-damaged units are not admitted.

rules.title: Used-vehicle age limit (about 5 years)
rules.rule_text: Iraq applies an age limit to used-vehicle imports, commonly cited around 5 years; some import guides report a stricter 2-year limit. Rules are enforced per entry point and change frequently — confirm the exact cut-off with the Umm Qasr agent / Iraqi customs before sourcing stock.
rules.notes: Sources conflict (5-year vs 2-year limit) — verify with Iraqi customs before purchase.

rules.title: Original Bill of Lading + vehicle identifiers
rules.rule_text: Vehicles must ship with the original Bill of Lading showing chassis number, engine number, cubic capacity, year of manufacture, brand, make and model. Duty varies by vehicle category and engine size, and by entry port (Umm Qasr, Basrah/Khor Al Zubair).
rules.source: Auto Beats LLC / One Roof Autos (Iraq import policy)
rules.notes: Duty varies by category and engine size — verify current schedule with Iraqi customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import policy documented
rules.rule_text: No dedicated EV import-duty relief has been identified in the sources reviewed; EVs are treated under the standard variable duty schedule. Confirm EV treatment with Iraqi customs before trading.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented in reviewed sources — verify with Iraqi customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) required
rules.rule_text: Ethiopia drives on the right and requires left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: EV-only import policy (petrol/diesel banned since Feb 2024)
rules.rule_text: Since February 2024 Ethiopia only allows the import of electric vehicles, banning petrol and diesel cars entirely. Combustion-engine used vehicles are not eligible for import or registration.
rules.source: Ethiopian Ministry of Finance (EV-only import policy, Feb 2024)
rules.notes: Policy change frequently cited; confirm current status with the Ethiopian Customs Commission.

rules.title: Used-vehicle age limit (about 5 years)
rules.rule_text: Used EV imports are subject to an age limit, commonly cited around 5 years (with 1–3 years preferred for quality). Age is counted from year of manufacture.
rules.notes: Age-limit figures vary by source — verify with Ethiopian customs before purchase.

rules.title: Original Bill of Lading + vehicle identifiers
rules.rule_text: Vehicles must ship with the original Bill of Lading showing chassis number, engine number, cubic capacity, year of manufacture, brand, make and model. Ethiopia is landlocked — vehicles transit via the Port of Djibouti.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Ethiopian customs before purchase.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Colombia drives on the right and requires left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Used vehicles generally not importable (new / current-year only)
rules.rule_text: Colombia generally restricts permanent import to brand-new vehicles (current year, 0 km). Used vehicles cannot be imported by non-diplomats; exceptions cover diplomats and classic/collector cars over 35 years old under special approval. Change-of-residence and free-zone regimes have separate rules.

rules.title: 1-year age limit (permitted categories)
rules.rule_text: For the limited categories that may import used vehicles, a 1-year age limit (from year of manufacture) generally applies. Used-vehicle imports are prohibited outside change-of-residence, diplomatic and free-zone regimes.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with DIAN before purchase.

rules.title: EV incentive (≈5–7% combined vs 35%+19% for ICE)
rules.rule_text: Colombia applies significant tax relief to electric vehicles — combined import taxes are reported around 5–7% of CIF for EVs, versus about 64–70% for combustion vehicles. The relief applies to new units; used-vehicle import remains prohibited.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify EV treatment with DIAN.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Morocco drives on the right and requires left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 5-year age limit + Euro 6 emissions
rules.rule_text: Imported used vehicles must be less than 5 years old at the moment of import and meet the Euro 6 emissions standard.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Moroccan Customs (ADII).

rules.title: Euro 6 conformity + standard documents
rules.rule_text: Vehicles must conform to Moroccan safety and environmental standards (Euro 6) and clear through Moroccan Customs (ADII) with invoice, bill of lading and certificate of origin.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with ADII.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief documented
rules.rule_text: No dedicated EV import-duty relief has been identified in the sources reviewed; EVs are subject to the same customs duty and VAT as combustion vehicles. Confirm EV treatment with ADII before trading.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented in reviewed sources — verify with ADII.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Sri Lanka drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. China-market LHD units cannot be registered as-is.

rules.title: Vehicle imports reopened (1 Feb 2025)
rules.rule_text: Sri Lanka lifted its multi-year vehicle import suspension effective 1 February 2025 under the Imports and Exports (Control) Regulations No. 01 of 2025 (Gazette Extraordinary No. 2421/04). Eligibility is determined under the new framework.
rules.notes: Regime changes frequently — verify current eligibility with Sri Lanka Customs.

rules.title: EV excise calculated per motor kW
rules.rule_text: Sri Lanka levies excise on electric vehicles per motor kilowatt (rather than per cc of engine displacement), under the February 2025 regime. EV duty treatment is distinct from combustion vehicles.
rules.notes: Rates change frequently by gazette — verify with Sri Lanka Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Turkey drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Layered tax: customs duty + ÖTV (SCT) + VAT
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles face a compounding stack — 10% customs duty, a Special Consumption Tax (ÖTV/SCT) that dominates the landed cost (90–100% for ICE engines up to 1600cc, up to 220% above 2000cc), then 20% VAT on the cumulative base. Chinese-origin petrol and hybrid vehicles attract an additional 50% tariff (raised from 40% in January 2025).
rules.notes: ÖTV/SCT brackets change frequently — verify with the Turkish Ministry of Trade before purchase.

rules.title: No universal age limit identified
rules.rule_text: No single universal used-vehicle age limit was identified in the sources reviewed; the import cost burden is driven by the ÖTV/SCT tax stack rather than an age cut-off. Confirm current used-vehicle eligibility with Turkish customs before sourcing stock.
rules.source: Needs verification (no explicit age rule located)
rules.notes: Used-vehicle eligibility not clearly documented — verify with Turkish customs.

rules.title: EV SCT (ÖTV) reduced brackets (25–75%)
rules.rule_text: Under Presidential Decision No. 10115 (24 July 2025), electric vehicles are taxed on a four-bracket Special Consumption Tax: 25% (≤160 kW and pre-tax price ≤1,650,000 TL), 55% (≤160 kW above the price threshold), 65% (>160 kW below threshold), 75% (>160 kW above threshold) — versus 90–100%+ for combustion engines. PHEVs are taxed at 45–85%.
rules.source: LenaCars (EV SCT brackets) / Presidential Decision No. 10115
rules.notes: Brackets depend on motor power and pre-tax price — verify with the Ministry of Trade.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) only
rules.rule_text: Malaysia drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. China-market LHD units cannot be registered as-is; source RHD export units.

rules.title: Approved Permit (AP) required
rules.rule_text: Used-vehicle import requires an Approved Permit (AP) issued by MITI under the Customs Act 1967. APs are restricted and priority is given to franchise holders; private used-vehicle import is heavily constrained.
rules.source: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI)
rules.notes: AP eligibility is restrictive — verify current AP requirements with MITI.

rules.title: Used-car age limit (1–5 years, AP-dependent)
rules.rule_text: Used imported vehicles generally carry a maximum age of about 1–5 years depending on the AP category. Age is counted from first registration to shipment month.
rules.notes: Age limit varies by AP category — verify with RMCD (Royal Malaysian Customs).

rules.title: EV import duty & excise relief (until 31 Dec 2025)
rules.rule_text: MITI grants temporary import-duty and excise relief on fully electric cars and motorcycles (until 31 December 2025), with an on-the-road price floor of RM100,000 for cars. The relief is not subject to the equivalent-engine-capacity condition. Confirm whether it has been extended for 2026.
rules.source: Ministry of Investment, Trade and Industry (MITI)
rules.notes: Temporary measure — verify current status (2026) with MITI.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) required
rules.rule_text: New Zealand requires right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. LHD vehicles cannot be registered except classics 20+ years old or under a Special Interest Vehicle (SIV) permit.

rules.title: No fixed age limit (standards-based)
rules.rule_text: New Zealand has no fixed age limit for used-vehicle imports; eligibility is instead set by emissions standards (models from ~2005 onward) and frontal-impact compliance (mandatory for MA/MB/MC vehicles built from October 2003).
rules.notes: Standards-based, not age-based — verify current standards with NZTA.

rules.title: Entry certification + biosecurity
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles require NZTA entry certification by an approved inspector, MPI biosecurity clearance (heat treatment/fumigation for brown marmorated stink bug during September–April), and pre-shipment inspection (e.g. JEVIC).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with NZTA and MPI.

rules.title: Clean Car Standard CO₂ charge (up to NZ$2,875)
rules.rule_text: New Zealand applies a Clean Car Standard CO₂ charge on high-emission imports (up to NZ$2,875; used cars calculated at half the new-car rate). Zero-tailpipe EVs do not incur the CO₂ charge, but pay 15% GST. Passenger cars are otherwise duty-free (0% customs duty).
rules.notes: CO₂ charge tiers change — verify current rates with NZTA / Waka Kotahi.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Algeria drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Used cars under 3 years old
rules.rule_text: Since 2023 Algeria has authorized individual import of used cars less than three years old. Under the 2025 Finance Law, imported cars under three years old may now be resold, but the tax benefits must be repaid on a sliding scale (100% if sold within 12 months of clearance, 66% within 12–24 months, 33% within 24–36 months).
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Algerian Customs (DGD).

rules.title: Safety equipment mandatory (ABS, airbags, speed limiter)
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must meet minimum safety standards including ABS and a speed limiter; vehicles over 1.2 litres additionally require two front airbags, headrests for all seats, windscreen/rear-window defrosters and child-seat anchors.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Algerian Customs.

rules.title: EV import-tax reduction (up to 80% personal channel)
rules.rule_text: Algeria applies import-tax reductions to electric vehicles — reported up to 80% on the personal-import channel (50% for petrol/hybrid up to 1800cc) under the 2025 regime. Customs duty is otherwise 15% (petrol ≤1800cc) or 30% (≥1800cc and EVs).
rules.notes: Reduction % varies by channel — verify with Algerian Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Qatar drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles under the GCC specification framework.
rules.source: Left- and right-hand traffic (Wikipedia) / Expat Focus

rules.title: 5-year age limit
rules.rule_text: Vehicles over 5 years old are prohibited from import into Qatar. Imports require a valid Qatar ID (residence permit) and Qatari driving licence.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Qatar Customs.

rules.title: GCC specification required
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must conform to GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) specification. Required documents include proof of ownership, registration certificate, purchase invoice, original Bill of Lading and prior insurance.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Qatar Customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Qatar in the sources reviewed; the flat 5% customs duty applies to all vehicles. EV adoption is supported through infrastructure rather than duty relief.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented in reviewed sources — verify with Qatar Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Azerbaijan drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 10-year age ban (Decree No. 94)
rules.rule_text: Since 28 April 2023 (Cabinet Decree No. 94), Azerbaijan bans the import of passenger cars manufactured more than 10 years ago — in 2026 that means model-year 2016 and newer. Every imported car must also have ABS, at least one airbag, and meet Euro-4 or higher emissions.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: Engine-cc excise + 18% VAT (no flat duty)
rules.rule_text: Azerbaijan levies an engine-capacity-based customs duty plus an engine-cc excise tax and 18% VAT (charged on CIF + excise). From January 2026, cars older than 7 years pay a higher excise coefficient (petrol 1.5×, diesel 2.0×). Clearance is via the Baku Single Window.
rules.notes: Excise is engine-cc based, not a single rate — verify with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: EV ≤3yr: 0% duty, no excise, but 18% VAT
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles three years old or newer pay 0% customs duty and no excise, but since 1 January 2026 are subject to 18% VAT like all other cars.
rules.notes: EV incentive applies to ≤3-year-old units — verify with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: Right-hand drive (RHD) required
rules.rule_text: Australia drives on the left and registers right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles. China-market LHD units cannot be registered as-is; source RHD export units (BYD, MG, GWM, Chery and others produce RHD for Australia).

rules.title: ROVER import approval mandatory (RVSA 2018)
rules.rule_text: Before importing a road vehicle, a Vehicle Import Approval must be obtained through ROVER under the Road Vehicle Standards Act 2018. Importing without approval is an offence. Used-vehicle pathways are narrow: the Specialist and Enthusiast Vehicle Scheme (SEVS), the 25-Year Rule, and the Personal Import Scheme (12+ months prior overseas ownership/use).
rules.notes: Approval pathways are restrictive — verify current SEVS/PIS eligibility with the Department of Infrastructure before sourcing.

rules.title: No blanket age limit (standards-based)
rules.rule_text: Australia has no blanket used-vehicle age limit; eligibility is instead set by Australian Design Rules (ADR) conformity, emissions and frontal-impact standards, and the import-approval pathway. Non-compliant or non-approved used vehicles cannot be registered.
rules.source: Australian Border Force (importing a motor vehicle)
rules.notes: Standards-based, not age-based — confirm ADR and approval pathway with ROVER.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief (LCT fuel-efficient threshold)
rules.rule_text: Australia grants no EV-specific import-duty relief; 5% customs duty and 10% GST apply to all passenger vehicles. Electric and other fuel-efficient vehicles (≤7L/100km) benefit from a higher Luxury Car Tax (LCT) threshold before the 33% LCT applies on the excess.
rules.source: Australian Taxation Office (Luxury Car Tax) / Australian Border Force
rules.notes: LCT thresholds are indexed annually — verify current figures with the ATO.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Russia drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Utilization (recycling) fee + EPTS activation
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles face a utilization (recycling) fee that escalated from 2024 and was further increased from 2025 (scrappage fees effectively doubled). Registration requires EPTS (electronic passport) activation. From 1 April 2024, Resolution 1291 closed the EAEU arbitrage loophole — cars cleared in Kyrgyzstan/Kazakhstan then imported into Russia pay the full domestic duty.
rules.notes: Utilization-fee amounts change frequently — verify current figures with the Federal Customs Service.

rules.title: Personal-import duty by engine cc + excise + 20% VAT
rules.rule_text: Personal import of a car into Russia is taxed by a combined customs-duty schedule keyed to engine displacement, plus an engine-power (horsepower) excise, plus 20% VAT, plus the utilization fee. Older and larger-engine vehicles attract higher charges.
rules.notes: Duty is engine-cc based, not a single rate — verify with the Federal Customs Service.

rules.title: No strict age limit identified (EAEU certification applies)
rules.rule_text: No single universal used-vehicle age limit was identified in the sources reviewed; eligibility is governed by EAEU technical certification and the utilization-fee + duty schedule, which rises for older vehicles. Confirm current used-vehicle eligibility with Russian customs.
rules.source: Needs verification (no explicit age rule located)
rules.notes: Used-vehicle eligibility not clearly documented — verify with the Federal Customs Service.

rules.title: No EV duty relief + EV/hybrid sanctions sensitivity
rules.rule_text: Russia grants no EV-specific import-duty relief; EVs still pay the utilization fee, VAT and applicable charges. Separately, EU sanctions ban the export of all new and second-hand electric and hybrid vehicles (and cars over 1,900cc) to Russia from the EU — a constraint that does not directly bind China-origin vehicles but signals the sanctions environment around EV/hybrid trade.
rules.notes: EV/hybrid treatment and sanctions scope change — verify before trading.

rules.title: Sanctions risk (recorded truthfully)
rules.rule_text: Russia is subject to EU/US sanctions. Western automakers (Volkswagen, BMW, etc.) prohibit exports to Russia and have contractual safeguards; luxury-car (>1,900cc) and EV/hybrid exports are banned from the EU. Chinese-origin vehicles are not directly sanctioned, but transactions face banking/payment/logistics friction and enhanced compliance scrutiny; gray-market routing of Western brands into Russia carries enforcement risk (account freezes, searches, prosecution).
rules.notes: Sanctions and compliance landscape changes frequently — obtain legal/compliance advice before trading.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) standard; RHD penalised
rules.rule_text: Georgia drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive (RHD) vehicles are not banned outright but face a tripled excise rate in every age bracket (a strong disincentive).
rules.source: Left- and right-hand traffic (Wikipedia) / CarSelect (RHD rate)
rules.notes: RHD excise triples in every age bracket — verify current rates with the Revenue Service.

rules.title: Nominal duty + per-cc excise + 18% VAT
rules.rule_text: Georgia runs one of the region's lightest customs regimes: import duty is nominal (about GEL 0.05 per cc plus 5% per year of age), plus a per-cc excise with a sharp age cliff at 6 years (1.5 GEL/cc under 6 years vs 4.5 GEL/cc over, as of April 2026), plus 18% VAT. RHD vehicles triple the excise.
rules.notes: Excise is per-cc with an age cliff — verify current brackets with the Revenue Service.

rules.title: 6-year excise cliff (not a ban)
rules.rule_text: Georgia walked back a planned ban on passenger vehicles older than 6 years and instead applies a tax: the per-cc excise steps up sharply at 6 years of age (about 1.5 GEL/cc to 4.5 GEL/cc). Older vehicles remain importable but carry a materially higher excise.
rules.notes: The 6-year threshold is a tax cliff, not a prohibition — verify current rates.

rules.title: EV exemption (0% duty + no excise, 18% VAT only)
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles are exempt from Georgia's import duty and per-cc excise, leaving 18% VAT as the main charge — a strong relief delta versus combustion vehicles. Euro 5 emission conformity applies to ICE imports.
rules.notes: EV exemption is source-backed — verify current status with the Revenue Service.

rules.title: Euro 5 emission conformity
rules.rule_text: Imported combustion vehicles must meet Euro 5 emission standards. Re-export through Poti/Batumi to Armenia, Azerbaijan and Central Asia may skip the tax if re-exported.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with the Revenue Service.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Tunisia drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Used cars under 5 years old
rules.rule_text: Since 2012 Tunisia has prohibited the entry of vehicles older than five years (an individual used-vehicle import must be no more than 5 years old). The imported vehicle requires an FCR (Fiche de Contrôle de Conformité) conformity certificate.
rules.source: US ITA Country Commercial Guide (trade.gov) / ElJaziraTransit
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Tunisian Customs.

rules.title: FCR conformity certificate required
rules.rule_text: Individual used-vehicle import requires a FCR (Fiche de Contrôle de Conformité) conformity certificate and the importer must be a Tunisian citizen aged 18+. High ICE tariffs plus 19% VAT and a consumption tax make combustion imports expensive.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Tunisian Customs.

rules.title: EV full exemption (0% duty + 0% VAT + 0% consumption)
rules.rule_text: Fully electric vehicles under 5 years old may pay 0% customs duty, 0% VAT and 0% consumption tax in Tunisia (2026) — one of the strongest EV relief packages in North Africa. This makes recent Chinese EVs the standout import category.
rules.notes: EV exemption is source-backed — verify current scope with Tunisian Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Oman drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles under GCC standard specifications.

rules.title: Private vehicles under 7 years old
rules.rule_text: Oman Customs permits import of private vehicles less than 7 years old (trucks/buses under 10 years, equipment under 15 years). The importer must be at least 18 years old for personal import, and vehicles must comply with the standard specifications in force in the Sultanate.
rules.source: Royal Oman Police — Directorate General of Customs
rules.notes: Official source — verify current age limits with Oman Customs.

rules.title: GCC standard specification required
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must comply with the standard specifications in force in the Sultanate (GCC specification). A flat 5% customs duty plus 5% VAT applies.
rules.source: Royal Oman Police — Directorate General of Customs
rules.notes: GCC specification is mandatory — verify with Oman Customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Oman in the sources reviewed; the flat 5% customs duty plus 5% VAT applies to all vehicles.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented in reviewed sources — verify with Oman Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Bahrain drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles under GCC specification.

rules.title: Age limit ~5 years (5–10 years pay BHD 1,000 fee)
rules.rule_text: Bahrain restricts imported vehicles to about 5 years of age; vehicles aged 5 to 10 years are subject to an additional flat import fee of BHD 1,000 (with heightened border scrutiny). Bahrain's parliament has considered extending the age limit from 5 to 10 years.
rules.source: JP Sheet (Bahrain import guide) / Expat Focus
rules.notes: Age-limit policy is in flux (5 vs 10 years) — verify with Bahrain Customs.

rules.title: GCC specification + 5% duty + 10% VAT
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must conform to GCC specification. Bahrain applies 5% customs duty plus 10% VAT (total ~15% on CIF + duty), the highest VAT in the GCC. Vehicles imported from other GCC countries with proof of prior duty payment may be exempt.
rules.notes: Verify current duty/VAT with Bahrain Customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Bahrain in the sources reviewed; the 5% customs duty plus 10% VAT applies. Bahrain has EV-adoption incentives, but their application to used imports is not confirmed in reviewed sources.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Bahrain Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Kuwait drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are generally not registrable.

rules.title: Used passenger cars ~5 years old
rules.rule_text: Kuwait restricts used private passenger-car imports to about five years from the date of manufacture — stricter than several other Gulf states. Confirm the current threshold with Kuwait Customs before sourcing stock.
rules.source: The Ship Cars (Kuwait import guide) / Kuwait Customs
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Kuwait General Administration of Customs before purchase.

rules.title: GCC specification conformity
rules.rule_text: Imported vehicles must conform to GCC (Gulf specification) standards covering climate-appropriate cooling, safety and emissions. Non-GCC-spec vehicles may require modification or assessment through Kuwait Customs and the Public Authority for Industry.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Kuwait Customs before purchase.

rules.title: 5% customs duty; no VAT
rules.rule_text: Kuwait applies a modest 5% customs duty on the assessed customs value for most passenger vehicles and has not implemented a broad-based VAT (no VAT applies to vehicle imports). Total import tax burden is comparatively light, provided age and specification requirements are met.
rules.source: The Ship Cars / JP Sheet (Kuwait import guide)
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Kuwait Customs before purchase.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Kuwait in the sources reviewed; the flat 5% duty applies to all vehicles. EV adoption is driven by charging infrastructure rather than duty relief.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Kuwait Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Armenia registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles only. Japanese domestic-market (RHD) cars cannot be registered in Armenia — source LHD export-spec units.

rules.title: EAEU Common Customs Tariff + 20% VAT
rules.rule_text: Armenia is an EAEU member and applies the EAEU Common Customs Tariff to non-EAEU vehicles: about 15% ad valorem for company (legal-entity) imports, plus 20% VAT on CIF + duty. Individuals importing for personal use instead pay an age- and engine-displacement (EUR-per-cc) unified customs payment.
rules.notes: Duty base differs by importer status (company % vs individual EUR-per-cc) — verify with the State Revenue Committee.

rules.title: Individual import: age/engine EUR-per-cc payment
rules.rule_text: For personal-use imports, Armenia charges a unified customs payment keyed to vehicle age and engine displacement (EUR-per-cc) rather than a flat percentage — so the effective duty is not a single number. Road tax and an environmental payment are also collected at entry.
rules.notes: EUR-per-cc basis scales with engine size and age — verify with the State Revenue Committee.

rules.title: EV 2026 duty-free quota + VAT exemption
rules.rule_text: In 2026 electric vehicles benefit from an EAEU 15,000-unit duty-free import quota plus a VAT exemption running through 31 December 2026 (duty exemption for permanent residents; EVs built 2024–2026) — a strong relief delta versus the ~15% duty + 20% VAT on combustion vehicles.
rules.notes: EV quota + VAT exemption runs to 31 Dec 2026 — verify current status with the State Revenue Committee.

rules.title: Landlocked — transit via Poti (Georgia) to Yerevan
rules.rule_text: Armenia is landlocked. The main corridor is sea freight to Poti (Georgia), then bonded overland transit through Georgia (Bagratashen/Sadakhlo) to Yerevan. EAEU-sourced vehicles may instead use the Upper Lars corridor from Russia.
rules.notes: Transit routing is operational guidance, not regulation — confirm with a forwarder.

rules.title: No strict age limit identified
rules.rule_text: No single universal used-vehicle age limit was identified for Armenia in the sources reviewed; eligibility is governed by EAEU certification and the age/engine-size duty schedule (which rises for older vehicles). Confirm current used-vehicle eligibility with the State Revenue Committee.
rules.source: Needs verification (no explicit age rule located)
rules.notes: Used-vehicle age eligibility not clearly documented — verify with the State Revenue Committee.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: The Dominican Republic drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 5-year age limit (cars); 15 years (trucks)
rules.rule_text: Under Law 04-07 (5 Jan 2007), used passenger cars more than five years old (from manufacture) may not be imported; trucks and heavy vehicles are limited to fifteen years. In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2021 and newer for passenger cars.
rules.notes: Age rule enforced at inspection — verify current cut-off with the DGA before purchase.

rules.title: Salvage vehicles prohibited (Decree 671-02)
rules.rule_text: Decree 671 of 27 Aug 2002 prohibits the importation of salvage vehicles (collision, theft-recovered, flood or otherwise damaged units). A clean, lien-free title is required.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with the DGA before purchase.

rules.title: 20% duty + 18% ITBIS + 17% first-plate
rules.rule_text: Vehicle imports face a layered tax stack: 20% customs duty on value, 18% ITBIS (VAT), and a first-registration (placa) tax of 17% of the CIF value scaled by CO₂ emissions under Law 253-12, plus a circulation tax (marbete) and a 2% transfer cost. Combined burden can approach or exceed half the vehicle value.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with the DGA before purchase.

rules.title: EV / hybrid reduced duties (evolving)
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles and hybrids have historically enjoyed reduced import duties under clean-energy incentives; the current 2026 scope should be confirmed with the DGA, as the policy framework has been evolving.
rules.notes: EV incentive scope evolving — verify current status with the DGA.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Ecuador drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 1-year age limit — used imports effectively prohibited
rules.rule_text: Ecuador allows imported vehicles up to roughly one year old (counted from the year of manufacture); used-vehicle imports are effectively prohibited, with diplomatic and returning-migrant cases as the only exceptions.
rules.notes: Used-car imports restricted — verify current conditions with SENAE before purchase.

rules.title: INEN conformity certificate (prior control)
rules.rule_text: Vehicle imports require an INEN Certificado de Conformidad / Reconocimiento (Servicio Ecuatoriano de Normalización) filed with the customs declaration via the VUE — a prior-control document issued for the model or model family.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with SENAE/INEN before purchase.

rules.title: ~34% duty + 10% excise + 15% VAT (~70% combined)
rules.rule_text: Combustion-vehicle imports face a compounding stack: ~34% customs duty, ~10% excise (ICE) on CIF + duty, 15% VAT on the cumulative base, plus para-fiscal levies — roughly 60–80% of CIF combined. ICE is assessed against the official retail price (PVP), not the invoice.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with SENAE before purchase.

rules.title: EV incentive (~0.5–2% vs ~70% ICE)
rules.rule_text: Electric vehicles attract a dramatically lower combined tax of roughly 0.5–2% of CIF (versus ~60–80% for combustion vehicles), but BEV duty/VAT relief requires a Ministry-of-Environment exemption approval. The incentive favors new EV units since used imports are effectively prohibited.
rules.notes: BEV relief needs environmental approval — verify current scope with SENAE.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Uruguay drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: Used cars over 10 years restricted
rules.rule_text: Uruguay restricts import of used cars more than 10 years old. Project cargo and machinery follow standard tariff rules with no age gate.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Dirección Nacional de Aduanas before purchase.

rules.title: Returning-citizen-only imports (Law 18.250 / Decree 330/2008)
rules.rule_text: Under Law 18.250 and Decree 330/2008, only returning Uruguayan citizens (with at least 12 months of prior vehicle use and 2 years' residence abroad) may import a used vehicle; private non-citizens and Uruguayan diplomats cannot import vehicles. The vehicle cannot be sold or transferred for 4 years.
rules.notes: Import eligibility is narrow (returning citizens) — verify with Dirección Nacional de Aduanas.

rules.title: Mercosur CET duty + 22% VAT
rules.rule_text: As a Mercosur member, Uruguay applies the bloc's Common External Tariff to extra-zone goods (tariff by HS code), plus 22% VAT (IVA) on the duty-inclusive value and first-registration charges.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Dirección Nacional de Aduanas.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Uruguay in the sources reviewed; the Mercosur CET duty plus 22% VAT applies. Uruguay promotes EV adoption through local incentives that do not reduce used-vehicle import duty.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Dirección Nacional de Aduanas.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Panama does not allow the import of right-hand-drive vehicles for road registration; left-hand-drive (LHD) only. This is enforced consistently with no widely recognised exceptions for passenger cars.

rules.title: Age limit conflicting (5 / 7 / 10 years cited)
rules.rule_text: Panama's vehicle age restriction is cited inconsistently across sources (five, seven or ten years from manufacture), and enforcement appears to vary by port and inspector. Verify the current threshold with a Panamanian customs broker before shipping any near-limit vehicle.
rules.notes: Conflicting age limits across sources — verify with ANA Panama before purchase.

rules.title: Clean title required (salvage rejected)
rules.rule_text: The vehicle must have a clear, lien-free title in the importer's name. Salvage titles, rebuilt titles and vehicles with unresolved liens are likely to be rejected or face significant complications at customs.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with ANA Panama before purchase.

rules.title: Colón Free Zone + Pensionado duty exemption
rules.rule_text: Panama operates the Colón Free Zone, a major regional re-export hub where goods (including vehicles) can enter duty-free for re-export. Qualifying Pensionado retirement-visa holders may claim an import-duty exemption on one personal vehicle every two years. A clean US export declaration and certificate of origin are part of the document pack.
rules.notes: Pensionado exemption and Free Zone treatment are scheme-specific — verify with ANA Panama.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Panama in the sources reviewed; the standard duty plus ITBMS applies. EV adoption is growing but driven by local incentives rather than import-duty relief.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with ANA Panama.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) market; RHD JDM permitted until 2030
rules.rule_text: Mongolia is a left-hand-drive market, but right-hand-drive Japanese domestic-market vehicles are currently permitted with a valid import licence. A complete ban on importing right-hand-drive vehicles is scheduled to take effect on 1 June 2030. China-market LHD units are directly registrable.
rules.notes: RHD ban scheduled 1 June 2030 — confirm current status with Mongolian Customs.

rules.title: No fixed age limit (tax rises with age)
rules.rule_text: Mongolia has no fixed vehicle-age cut-off for used imports, but excise and duty generally climb with vehicle age — so the newest unit the budget allows is usually the cheaper option once taxes are counted. Confirm the current age-based schedule with Mongolian Customs before committing.
rules.notes: No hard cut-off; tax climbs with age — verify the current schedule with Mongolian Customs.

rules.title: 5% customs duty + 10% VAT + excise
rules.rule_text: Mongolia applies roughly a 5% customs duty plus 10% VAT, plus an excise tax that runs from MNT 750,000 to MNT 65,975,000 depending on engine size and age. An additional 33% excise applies to the portion of a vehicle's customs value exceeding MNT 360 million. Duty is assessed on the CIF value.
rules.notes: Excise is engine-size and age based — verify with Mongolian Customs before purchase.

rules.title: EV / hybrid / gas vehicles get up to 50% excise discount
rules.rule_text: Hybrid, electric and gas-fuelled vehicles receive up to a 50% discount on excise tax in Mongolia, a meaningful relief delta versus combustion vehicles. This makes recent Chinese EVs and hybrids particularly attractive on the tax side.
rules.notes: Up to 50% excise discount for EV/hybrid/gas — confirm current scope with Mongolian Customs.

rules.title: Landlocked — transit via Tianjin then rail
rules.rule_text: Mongolia is landlocked. Vehicles transit by sea to Tianjin (China), then continue by rail to Ulaanbaatar via the Erlian/Zamyn-Üüd border crossing. Customs clearance is completed at the Ulaanbaatar rail terminal.
rules.notes: Transit routing is operational guidance — confirm with a forwarder.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Kyrgyzstan drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 10-year age limit
rules.rule_text: Used vehicles older than 10 years are not allowed to be imported into Kyrgyzstan. In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2016 and newer. Confirm the current threshold with the State Customs Service before sourcing older stock.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: EAEU member — Common Customs Tariff applies
rules.rule_text: Kyrgyzstan is an EAEU member and applies the bloc's Common Customs Tariff to non-EAEU vehicles. Permanent importation is subject to customs duty and VAT; temporary (employment-status) import has a distinct lower-charge treatment. No pre-shipment inspection is required.
rules.notes: EAEU framework; no inspection required — verify duty rates with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: EV import-duty treatment needs verification
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Kyrgyzstan in the sources reviewed. Kyrgyzstan is an EAEU member, so EV treatment may follow the EAEU framework; confirm current EV duty with the State Customs Service before trading.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Serbia drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive imports are generally not registrable.

rules.title: Euro 3 emission standard minimum
rules.rule_text: All imported vehicles must meet the Euro 3 emission standard or higher. Petrol, diesel, hybrid and electric (EV) fuel types are all accepted by Serbian Customs.
rules.notes: Euro 3 minimum — confirm current emission threshold with Serbian Customs.

rules.title: No fixed age limit
rules.rule_text: Serbia has no fixed vehicle-age cut-off for used imports; the binding gate is the Euro 3 emission standard and technical condition. Damaged vehicles may be imported if repairable with minimal work.
rules.notes: No age limit — eligibility is standards-based. Verify with Serbian Customs.

rules.title: 12.5% duty + 20% VAT (AMSS catalog basis)
rules.rule_text: Serbia charges 12.5% customs duty on non-EU origin vehicles (0% only for EU origin with EUR1/origin declaration) plus 20% VAT on the customs value plus duty. Customs uses the AMSS catalog value to calculate taxes regardless of the actual purchase price.
rules.notes: AMSS catalog value is the tax base — verify current rates with Serbian Customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty relief was identified for Serbia in the sources reviewed; EVs are accepted but face the same 12.5% duty plus 20% VAT as other vehicles. Serbia imports around 130,000 used cars annually, with growing hybrid interest.
rules.notes: No EV-specific relief — verify current EV treatment with Serbian Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) market
rules.rule_text: Senegal drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are generally not suitable for permanent registration.

rules.title: 3-year age rule (private); 6-year (commercial)
rules.rule_text: Imported used vehicles for private use must not be more than 3 years old from original registration and not more than 4 years from the year of manufacture. Commercial vehicles must not be more than 60 months from original registration and not more than 6 years from manufacture. In 2026 this makes roughly model-year 2023 and newer eligible for private use.
rules.notes: Strict age rule (3yr private / 6yr commercial) — verify with Senegal Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Pre-shipment inspection in country of origin
rules.rule_text: All used vehicles imported into Senegal must undergo pre-delivery inspection in the country of origin before shipment. Required documents include bill of lading, certificate of origin, import licence/approval permit (obtained before departure), original title and purchase invoice.
rules.notes: Pre-shipment inspection and prior import approval are mandatory — verify with Senegal Customs.

rules.title: EV import-duty treatment needs verification
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Senegal in the sources reviewed. EV policy is developing; confirm current EV duty with Senegal Customs before trading.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Senegal Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Côte d'Ivoire drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: 5-year age limit (cars)
rules.rule_text: Côte d'Ivoire restricts imported cars (tourism vehicles) to a maximum of 5 years of age. Taxis are also 5 years, minibuses (9–34 seats) 7 years, buses (34+ seats) 10 years, and trucks up to 10 years depending on weight. In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2021 and newer for passenger cars.
rules.notes: 5-year car limit — verify current threshold with Côte d'Ivoire Customs before purchase.

rules.title: ~53% customs duty + registration fee
rules.rule_text: Côte d'Ivoire charges approximately 53% customs duty on the vehicle CIF value, plus a vehicle registration fee of about EUR 690 per vehicle. Vehicles cannot be shipped in the same container as household goods or personal effects.
rules.notes: ~53% duty is an approximation — verify with Côte d'Ivoire Customs.

rules.title: EV import-duty treatment needs verification
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Côte d'Ivoire in the sources reviewed; EVs are expected to follow the standard ~53% schedule. Confirm current EV treatment with Côte d'Ivoire Customs.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Côte d'Ivoire Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Cameroon drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles; left-hand-drive imports are common and no fixed age limit applies.

rules.title: No fixed age limit
rules.rule_text: Cameroon has no fixed vehicle-age limit for used imports; new and used vehicles are both accepted. Taxes may vary depending on the vehicle's age, engine power and other factors.
rules.source: Japan Carrier / Qualitex Trading (Cameroon import regulations)
rules.notes: No fixed age limit — but taxes vary by age/engine. Verify with Cameroon Customs.

rules.title: 58% (≤2000cc) / 77% (>2000cc) duty
rules.rule_text: Cameroon charges import duty of 58% of CIF for vehicles with engine capacity below 2000cc and 77% of CIF for engines above 2000cc, plus a non-sale certificate is required. Documents must be submitted at least one month before shipment arrival.
rules.notes: Engine-capacity-based duty (58% / 77%) — verify with Cameroon Customs.

rules.title: EV import-duty treatment needs verification
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Cameroon in the sources reviewed. Cameroon's duty is engine-capacity based, so EV classification is unclear; confirm with Cameroon Customs before trading.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented — verify with Cameroon Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Lebanon drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are not registrable — a China-market LHD unit imports directly.

rules.title: 8-year age limit
rules.rule_text: Lebanon prohibits the import of used vehicles older than eight years (from the year of manufacture). In 2026 this means roughly model-year 2018 and newer.
rules.notes: Uncertain / changes frequently — verify with Lebanese Customs before purchase.

rules.title: Diesel used vehicles prohibited
rules.rule_text: Lebanon prohibits the import of used vehicles that use diesel fuel. Petrol, hybrid and electric powertrains are admissible.
rules.notes: Diesel ban — verify current scope with Lebanese Customs.

rules.title: Bill of lading, registration, title and invoice
rules.rule_text: Required documents include the original bill of lading (make, model, engine and chassis numbers, weight and colour), original vehicle registration, original certificate of title and a purchase/commercial invoice.
rules.notes: Standard documentation — verify with Lebanese Customs.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Lebanon in the sources reviewed; EVs follow the standard duty schedule (flat 5M LBP up to 20M LBP CIF, or 50% above). Confirm current EV treatment with Lebanese Customs.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with Lebanese Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Ukraine drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are not registrable.

rules.title: Euro-2 emission standard minimum
rules.rule_text: Imported passenger cars must meet the Euro-2 environmental standard or higher (Euro-2 was introduced in 1995). Vehicles from a state recognised by Ukraine as an occupier/aggressor are excluded.
rules.source: Law of Ukraine No. 2612-VIII / CARGO LINE
rules.notes: Euro-2 minimum — verify current standard with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: No hard age cap today; 20-year cap proposed
rules.rule_text: Ukraine has no firm vehicle-age cut-off at present (Euro-2 compliance is the binding gate), but a maximum import age of 20 years has been proposed. Confirm the current rule with the State Customs Service before sourcing older stock.
rules.notes: Proposed 20-year cap — not yet confirmed as law. Verify with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: Certificate of Conformity + preliminary declaration
rules.rule_text: Clearance requires a Certificate of Conformity for an individually approved wheeled vehicle, a preliminary customs declaration with a financial guarantee of the customs payments, and standard documents (registration certificate, invoice, export declaration, payment receipt, passport and TIN).
rules.source: CARGO LINE (Ukraine customs clearance) / Law No. 2612-VIII
rules.notes: Confirm the document set with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: Full EV exemption ends 31 Dec 2025
rules.rule_text: Ukraine's full EV import exemptions (0% duty, 0% excise, 0% VAT) expired on 31 December 2025. From 2026 electric vehicles pay up to 10% import duty, an excise of €1 per kWh of battery capacity, and 20% VAT — erasing the previous EV cost advantage.
rules.notes: EV exemption ended Dec 2025 — verify current EV treatment with the State Customs Service.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Belarus drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: No hard age ban (rate scales with age)
rules.rule_text: Belarus has no hard vehicle-age cut-off for used imports; the individual unified customs rate scales up steeply with age and engine size (and a per-cc minimum applies).
rules.notes: No hard age ban — but older cars cost materially more in unified rate. Verify with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: EAEU member — single customs clearance
rules.rule_text: Belarus is an EAEU member. A vehicle cleared and registered in Belarus moves across the EAEU (Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Armenia) without re-paying customs duty. Russia still levies a recycling fee on EAEU-origin vehicles.
rules.notes: EAEU single-clearance advantage; Russia recycling fee applies on re-export. Verify with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: EV duty-free quota (20,000 units) + 0% EV VAT
rules.rule_text: Belarus keeps a 20,000-unit duty-free import quota for pure electric vehicles in 2026 (13,800 for companies, 6,200 for individuals). Individual pure-EV import VAT stays at 0% through 31 December 2028 (Decree No. 428). Hybrids are excluded and pay 15% duty + 20% VAT.
rules.notes: Quota is limited and resets annually; over 40% used by April 2026. Verify quota status with the State Customs Committee.

rules.title: Landlocked — transit via Klaipėda/Riga or Brest
rules.rule_text: Belarus is landlocked. Vehicles arrive overland via Poland (Brest border) or through the Klaipėda (Lithuania) and Riga (Latvia) seaports, then by road to Minsk for customs clearance.
rules.notes: Transit routing is operational guidance — confirm with a forwarder.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Bolivia drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. Right-hand-drive vehicles are not registrable.

rules.title: Very strict age rule (~1 model year)
rules.rule_text: Bolivia applies one of the region's strictest used-vehicle age rules: since December 2014 the maximum age for imported cars is one model year old (some sources cite up to two years). In 2026 this means only brand-new or current-model-year units qualify — a near-total bar to used imports.
rules.source: US trade.gov (Bolivia trade barriers) / Bolivian Customs
rules.notes: Sources conflict (1 vs 2 years vs ~10 years). Verify the exact cut-off with Aduana Nacional before sourcing stock.

rules.title: NIT + licensed customs broker (Agente Despachante)
rules.rule_text: Bolivia is landlocked; vehicles transit via Iquique/Antofagasta (Chile) or Matarani/Ilo (Peru). Import requires a locally registered entity with NIT, and a licensed Agente Despachante is mandatory for all shipments above USD 1,000.
rules.notes: Landlocked transit + mandatory broker — verify with Aduana Nacional.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Bolivia in the sources reviewed; imports follow the NANDINA tariff plus an effective 14.94% IVA. Confirm EV treatment with Aduana Nacional.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented — verify with Aduana Nacional.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Costa Rica drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: No fixed age limit (duty rises with age)
rules.rule_text: Costa Rica has no fixed vehicle-age cut-off for used imports, but import tax rises sharply with age (52.29% ≤3 years, 63.91% at 4 years, 79.03% at 6+ years). Older vehicles also require more frequent RITEVE inspections.
rules.source: Vamos Rent A Car (Costa Rica import tax guide)
rules.notes: No age ban — but age drives the duty tier. Verify with Costa Rica Customs.

rules.title: RITEVE emissions/safety inspection
rules.rule_text: All imported vehicles must pass emissions and safety testing at RITEVE; vehicles over 10 years old require annual technical inspection (newer vehicles every two years).
rules.source: Vamos Rent A Car / US Embassy Costa Rica
rules.notes: RITEVE inspection required — verify with Costa Rica Customs.

rules.title: EV zero import tax (Law 9518); hybrids partial
rules.rule_text: Costa Rica exempts fully electric vehicles from import tax, sales tax and consumption tax under Law 9518 (fully electric vehicles under US$30,000 historically exempt; hybrids do not receive the full exemption).
rules.notes: EV zero import tax; hybrid treatment partial — verify with Costa Rica Customs.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Guatemala drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles.

rules.title: ~10-year age limit (cited inconsistently)
rules.rule_text: Sources cite a 10-year age limit (from date of manufacture) for used-vehicle imports into Guatemala, though the exact threshold is cited inconsistently and no definitive SAT regulation is publicly documented. Confirm with a Guatemalan customs broker.
rules.source: West Coast Shipping (Guatemala SAT vs reality guide)
rules.notes: Age limit cited inconsistently — verify with SAT / a licensed broker.

rules.title: DAI duty + 12% VAT + IPRIMA 20%
rules.rule_text: Guatemala applies the DAI import duty (0–15%, 0% under CAFTA-DR for US-built vehicles) plus 12% IVA, plus a first-registration IPRIMA tax of ~20% for vehicles carrying up to five people.
rules.source: West Coast Shipping / AB Group Shipping (Guatemala guides)
rules.notes: Layered DAI + IVA + IPRIMA; exact rates vary — verify with SAT.

rules.title: No EV-specific import-duty relief recorded
rules.rule_text: No EV-specific import-duty exemption was confirmed for Guatemala in the sources reviewed; EVs are expected to follow the standard DAI + IVA + IPRIMA stack. Confirm EV treatment with SAT.
rules.notes: EV treatment not documented for used imports — verify with SAT.

rules.title: Left-hand drive (LHD) only
rules.rule_text: Paraguay drives on the right and registers left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicles. A China-market LHD unit imports directly without conversion.

rules.title: 10-year age limit (Ley 2018/2002)
